questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: Identify an integer division bug in a ticket snippet
questions.stem:
A ticket reports this Java statement:
```java
int total = 7 / 2 + 1;
```
What is the actual bug in the expression?

options.text: Integer division truncates the remainder before any later arithmetic
options.misconception: Assumes the division yields a floating-point value before adding one

options.text: The variable is never initialized and causes a compile error
options.misconception: assumes local variables default to zero

options.text: The semicolon after the first statement is unnecessary
The plus operator binds tighter than division in Java

questions.explanation: Both operands of 7 / 2 are int, so Java performs integer division: 7 / 2 truncates to 3 before + 1 is applied, giving total = 4 rather than 3.5. Option B is wrong because this statement initializes total. Option C is wrong because the semicolon is the required statement terminator. Option D is wrong because / binds tighter than +, so no precedence reversal occurs - the truncation is the real defect.
questions.hint: Both operands are int - what does 7 / 2 evaluate to before the + 1?

questions.learningObjective: Select the true statement about Java primitive types
questions.stem:
Consider this declaration:
```java
char c = 'A';
```
Which statement about primitive types is true?

options.text: char stores a String of length one in Java
double and float have identical precision by default
boolean can hold 0 and 1 as numeric values
int is a 32-bit signed primitive type in Java

questions.explanation: Option D is true: int is a 32-bit signed primitive in Java, holding values from -2^31 to 2^31 - 1. Option A is wrong because char holds one 16-bit Unicode character, not a String. Option B is wrong because double is 64-bit while float is 32-bit, so their precision differs. Option C is wrong because boolean has only the values true and false, not the numeric values 0 and 1.
